memoryTip: Multi + farious forms — many varied kinds at once.
correctPassage: The archive's multifarious holdings span field notes, oral histories, and rare botanical sketches.
wrongPassages: Reviewers praised the report's multifarious focus on a single, narrowly defined case study.
The committee sought a multifarious policy that treated every district by the exact same rule.
Her multifarious wardrobe consisted of one navy blazer worn to every formal event.

definition: arranged in layers; divided into status levels
memoryTip: In strata (layers) — stacked rock or stacked social ranks.
correctPassage: Access to specialized care remained stratified by income, region, and insurance status.
wrongPassages: Geologists described the cliff as stratified after finding a single uniform deposit with no distinct bands.
They mixed the pigment until it was stratified into one smooth, undifferentiated color.
The firm insisted its workforce was stratified because every employee earned the same wage and title.

definition: having real importance or a firm basis
memoryTip: Has substance — real weight and importance, not fluff.
correctPassage: The board demanded substantive revisions to the budget, not cosmetic wording changes.
wrongPassages: They called the plan substantive even though it offered only vague slogans and no data.
They labeled the empty press release substantive for using elegant stationery and a formal seal.
A substantive edit left every flawed claim intact while adding several pages of filler.

memoryTip: A long step forward — or progress (“made great strides”).
correctPassage: Public health agencies made a significant stride in reducing childhood infection rates.
wrongPassages: After months of setbacks, the team celebrated a stride that returned them to the project's starting point.
Her stride across the stage was a sequence of tiny, hesitant shuffles between the microphones.
Missing every milestone was treated as a stride toward completing the product on schedule.

definition: proceeding gradually and subtly with harmful effects
memoryTip: In-side-ious: harm sneaks in from inside before you notice.
correctPassage: An insidious form of measurement bias can quietly distort results long before anyone notices.
wrongPassages: The hazard was insidious: alarms sounded and warning signs marked every entrance in bright red.
Colleagues trusted his insidious candor, which left motives open and tricks impossible.
They welcomed the insidious reform that openly corrected every flaw in a single afternoon.
